family.tagline: A bookkeeper, a device consultant and one Companion Core by the sea.
family.story: Agnieszka runs a bookkeeping and HR service from the writing desk upstairs. Tomasz, an IoT consultant, works at the octagonal table in the sunroom. One Companion Core on a shelf there serves both businesses.

members.name: Agnieszka
members.work: runs a bookkeeping and HR service

companion.name: Truffle
companion.job: Opens Twenty in its own browser and moves the deals Agnieszka names.
companion.limits: Prepares entries only. Agnieszka checks every field before it stands.

companion.name: Gadget
companion.job: Drafts the handover notes Tomasz sends to clients after an install.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Tomasz reads every note and sends it himself.

popup.title: Tomasz carries the Core in
popup.body: Up the broad timber steps, a parcel waits at the double doors. Tomasz carries the Companion Core to the sunroom shelf Agnieszka has cleared.

popup.title: Agnieszka lifts out the Core
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Agnieszka sets the Core on its shelf, in sight of the door.

popup.title: One press wakes the Core
popup.body: Tomasz plugs in the cable and Agnieszka presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: The phone finds the Core
popup.body: Agnieszka opens the Wi-Fi settings on her phone and joins the Core’s own network. Then she chooses the home network.

popup.title: Pick the first agent and apps
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Agnieszka picks OpenClaw, and the couple add Nextcloud and Forgejo. Then they walk away.

beats.capability: an agent with its own browser, running in its own sandbox on your Core

popup.title: Truffle says hello
popup.body: Agnieszka greets the agent she named Truffle. Truffle answers from the Core on its shelf.

say.speaker: agnieszka
say.text: Good morning, Agnieszka. Truffle here. Which client first?

beats.capability: read ebooks in your browser, with notes and highlights; your library lives on your Core

popup.title: Agnieszka picks up where she stopped
popup.body: After lunch, Agnieszka stretches along the sectional with a thick biography from the family’s ebook library. Koodo Reader keeps her place and her margin notes on the Core.

beats.capability: host your own Git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: A client’s settings get a branch
popup.body: Before a client’s install, Tomasz saves her sensor settings as a branch, so any change can be undone. Forgejo keeps that history on the Core.

beats.capability: a chat interface wired to the local model on your Core

popup.title: The gappy log gets a question
popup.body: A client’s sensor log is full of gaps. Tomasz sorts it in JupyterLab, then asks a model through Open WebUI. The question stays on the Core by default.

beats.capability: an agent that talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Gadget drafts, and Tomasz sends
popup.body: After an install, Tomasz messages Gadget his notes. Gadget drafts the handover on the Core’s local model, and Tomasz reads it and sends it himself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: tomasz
say.text: Here is the handover note. Please read it before you send it.

beats.capability: a shared household hub for notes, shopping, chores and expenses

popup.title: Agnieszka gives Tomasz the deck oiling
popup.body: The deck needs oil before the weather turns. Agnieszka adds it to the HomeHub chore board and gives it to Tomasz. The board is served from the Core.

beats.capability: a shared household hub with a recipe book, a shopping list and an expiry tracker

popup.title: The oldest mackerel goes first
popup.body: A neighbour’s boat lands more mackerel than the street can eat. Agnieszka dates the spare bags in HomeHub’s expiry tracker on the Core, so the oldest gets cooked first.

beats.capability: control and automate your smart home from one place, locally

popup.title: Tomasz measures the warm sunroom
popup.body: The sunroom runs warm, so Tomasz puts a Wi-Fi sensor there and one in the kitchen. Home Assistant compares both readings on the Core and itself needs no cloud account.

beats.capability: fill and sign PDF forms on any device, from your own Core

popup.title: A client signs at the table
popup.body: The boatyard’s owner comes by on Wednesday morning. She signs the engagement letter on her phone, over the home Wi-Fi, with Docuseal on the Core. Agnieszka pours the tea.

beats.capability: budget around recurring expenses by setting money aside for upcoming bills and goals

popup.title: Money set aside for the van
popup.body: The van’s service and the software renewals land in one month. At the dining table Tomasz sets money aside in monetr, which keeps the budget on the Core.

beats.capability: your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: The payroll run finds its folder
popup.body: A client’s payroll run lists her staff’s wages. Agnieszka files it in Nextcloud, on the Core, not in a rented drive.

beats.capability: keep customers, deals and custom fields in a CRM you host yourself

popup.title: Truffle moves the boatyard along
popup.body: The boatyard has signed. Agnieszka asks Truffle to move the deal along, and Truffle opens Twenty on the Core. Agnieszka checks the new stage herself before the deal moves on.

say.speaker: agnieszka
say.text: The stage is ready. Please check it before it moves on.

beats.capability: connect your apps with visual automations

popup.title: A report lands where Agnieszka looks
popup.body: Each Friday morning, an Activepieces flow Tomasz built gathers the clients’ device reports for Agnieszka. It runs on the Core, and she finds them ready when she bills.

beats.capability: invoicing, expenses, customers and profit and loss for a small business

popup.title: The boatyard gets its first invoice
popup.body: This week the boatyard’s first invoice goes out. Agnieszka raises it in Akaunting on the Core, beside her other clients’ invoices and expenses.

beats.capability: the LibreOffice suite in your browser

popup.title: A new client’s handbook takes shape
popup.body: A new client wants a staff handbook before the month ends. Agnieszka drafts it in LibreOffice, which runs on the Core and shows in her browser.

beats.capability: stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: Tomasz finds the album from breakfast
popup.body: After a client call, Tomasz takes his phone to the deck bench and searches for the album Agnieszka mentioned. Navidrome serves it from the Core over the home Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: a local video recorder with object detection for your IP cameras

popup.title: Tomasz draws the drive’s edge
popup.body: Passing cars on the lane keep starting clips, so Tomasz draws a zone around his own drive in Frigate. The clips stay on the Core.

popup.title: Two businesses, one shelf
popup.body: Payroll files, sensor settings and drive clips sit on one Companion Core, on a shelf in the sunroom.

closing.body: Your client files, invoices and device settings can sit on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: No TV, screen or fireplace in this home: the media beat is living-read at the couch (Koodo Reader). No text says TV or screen.
Bedroom 2 has the only desk (the writing desk): Agnieszka’s anchors are that desk, then the room. Tomasz sits at the octagonal table in the Sunroom Lounge (dining-table, room living).
garden-zone assumes the family fitted their own IP camera over the garage door: it is not in the Core box or the 3D scene. Frigate: no detection claim, nothing prevented.

Truffle is OpenClaw (ftue-hello and desk-deal open apps on the Core only: no website). Gadget is Hermes; table-gadget is the first Hermes beat and carries the chat-service note. Tomasz sends every note.
Docuseal is spelled as the catalog does. The client signs on her phone over the home Wi-Fi, so no outside signer needs the Core. No legal claim; Akaunting carries no accounting advice.

Apps over the fleet 40 percent cap (immich, hortusfox, paperless, vaultwarden) were left out. table-notebook: Open WebUI carries the chip, JupyterLab is the companion; the question stays on the Core by default.
desk-flow names no Nextcloud step: the Activepieces listing does not promise one.
desk-handbook (LibreOffice) is the one office-suite beat, no feature claim. kitchen-sensors sits on the second counter run; the dining beats use the nook and dining room tables.
